Which fundamental right is guaranteed by the Constitution of India as mentioned in the paragraph ?
opts: The right to free and compulsory education
The right to freedom of speech
The right to work and employment
context: There are several other fields in which it is desirable that a clear policy should be laid down on an all-India basis. One of the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution is the right of every citizen of the Union to free and compulsory education up to the age of 14. For the proper functioning of democracy, the Centre must see that every individual is equipped with the necessary knowledge, skill and aptitudes to discharge his duties as a responsible and co-operative citizen. What James Madison said about his country, the United States, many years ago, holds good today in our country also. "A popular Government without popular information or the means of acquiring it is but a prologue to a farce of tragedy or perhaps both. Knowledge will forever govern ignorance, and the people who mean to be their own governors must arm themselves with the power which knowledge gives." We should, however like to add that it is not only knowledge that is required, but also the right kind of social training and the inculcation of right ideals without which knowledge by itself may be sterile or worse. Training for democracy postulates a balanced education in which social virtues, intellectual development and practical skill all receive due consideration and the pattern of such an education must be envisaged on an all-India basis.
